Subject: BrightLedger DPA draft (Round 1 redlines)

Diego —

Thanks for sending over the baseline DPA. Attached are BrightLedger's a few targeted redlines and a short cover note from our privacy counsel (PDF). High level: we are primarily focused on tightening subprocessors, adding a clear transfer mechanism for EU data, and a slightly shorter retention carveout for analytics. I flagged a couple of clauses where we need clarity on caching behavior and KV cache lifetime (our infra team is concerned about persisted tokens).

Key asks:
- Explicit subprocessors list + 30-day prior notice for new subs
- EU transfer language: add SCCs or equivalent in the Annex (we can accept SCCs)
- Limitations on retention: 180 days for logs and telemetry unless otherwise agreed

Attached: BrightLedger_DPA_redlines_v1.docx and privacy counsel notes (PDF). Can you confirm Redwood's position on notice timing for new subprocessors and whether you can commit to SCCs in the Annex?

If easier, we can do a 30-min call later this week with Peter (cc'd).

Thanks,
Emma Jay
Head of Legal Ops
BrightLedger Inc.

Emma —

Appreciate the thorough notes and the redlines. I took a quick pass and looped in Marissa (privacy/product counsel) and Neha (security/compliance) to verify the operational details on caching and subprocessors. High-level answers below; we'll follow up with specifics in a marked-up DPA by EOD Wednesday.

Quick responses to your asks:
- New subprocessors: Redwood provides notice for new subprocessors and an opportunity to object; our standard is 30 days' notice for material subs. I'll confirm whether we can commit to a formal 30-day prior consent window vs. objection-rights.
- EU transfers: Redwood supports SCCs and we can include the standard SCC Annex; we'll confirm the exact language and whether we need any additional safeguards for specific data categories.
- Retention: We typically retain logs/telemetry for 365 days by default (operational + quality monitoring). We can offer a 180-day option for contractually-limited customers; will propose language to reflect that as an option.

Let's tentatively schedule a 30-minute call with you + Peter on Thursday 1/28 11:00am PT to walk through open items. Does that work?

I'll attach a first internal-marked DPA once we finalize responses.

Best,
Diego Fernandez

Diego / team —

Forwarding BrightLedger's redlines and counsel notes. Summary of Marissa's quick locus:
- Subprocessor notice: we generally provide notice and an object window; customers can require a longer notice in enterprise deals but it is negotiable. Recommend offering 30 days' notice with a requirement that objections are specific and based on materiality.
- SCCs: Agree to include SCCs in Annex A. We'll add a clause that the SCCs attach to the DPA and that the Controller/Processor roles are clarified per Annex.
- Retention: push back on hard 180 days for logs — propose language: "Retention of operational logs and telemetry shall be limited to 180 days where Customer elects the 'reduced-retention' option; otherwise standard retention applies." This gives commercial flexibility.

Operational items for Neha: please confirm whether we can produce a one-page list of current subprocessors to attach, and whether any of the infra caching paths persist PII beyond the request lifetime.

Also: recommend we prepare a redline with two tracks: (1) baseline (Redwood standard), (2) commercial (contractual concessions for BrightLedger). Will draft and send tonight.

Marissa
Sr. Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 28 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: BrightLedger DPA draft (privacy counsel comments)

Diego / Emma —

Thanks for scheduling. Attached are a couple of annotated points from Transaction Labs that are non-negotiable from BrightLedger's perspective and a list of suggested alternative language where we think Redwood's standard clause is too broad. Highlights:
- Subprocessors: BrightLedger requires 30 days' prior written notice for additions to the subprocessor list for categories that process Customer Personal Data; Redwood's object/consent approach is acceptable only if the customer has an explicit objection mechanism tied to materiality and a right to terminate if critical (we flagged suggested termination language).
- International transfers: SCCs in the Annex are fine; counsel asks for a short declaration that Redwood will execute supplementary technical/organizational measures in the event of any changes to transfer law.
- Security logging: request to limit retention for session logs to 180 days unless Customer agrees in writing to longer retention for troubleshooting.

I attached a PDF of our marked notes: BrightLedger_privacy_counsel_comments.pdf. Happy to walk through during the call — agenda: subprocessors, SCC Annex, and retention.

Best,
Peter Hsu
Partner, Privacy & Data Protection
Transaction Labs (external counsel to BrightLedger)
